paraphrase: When the Śaiva secrets were lost at the start of the Kali age, Śiva as Śrīkaṇṭha urged the sage Durvāsas to preserve them; Durvāsas created a mind-born son, Tryambakāditya; fourteen mind-born siddhas followed; the fifteenth married a brāhmaṇa woman; their descendant Saṅgamāditya came to Kashmir, followed by Varṣāditya, Aruṇāditya, Ānanda and Somānanda, who composed the Śivadṛṣṭi; this Tryambaka lineage ('Terambā') spread as a maṭhikā.
